Record date: 2129-08-21
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 08/21/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Persistent shortness of breath and continued lower extremity edema despite treatment adjustments.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up after one week on the revised treatment regimen. He reports slight improvement in his shortness of breath, particularly during activities of daily living, but continues to experience significant dyspnea at rest. The productive cough remains unchanged, with yellow-green sputum production persisting. Mr. Fairfax notes that while the increased furosemide has led to some reduction in edema, he still experiences discomfort and swelling extending to the thighs.
He expresses ongoing fatigue and frustration with sleep disturbances, stating that the sleep study referral has yet to be scheduled. He denies fever but continues to experience chills and malaise intermittently.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, - weight gain, + chills, - night sweats. Pulmonary - + shortness of breath at rest, + productive cough with yellow-green sputum, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 150/88 mmHg - Heart Rate: 88 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 24 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 87% on room air
General: The patient appears fatigued, in moderate respiratory distress, utilizing accessory muscles for breathing.
HEENT: No nasal flaring, oropharynx clear.
Lungs: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, with wheezing and bilateral crackles noted throughout.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops.
Extremities: Marked bilateral lower extremity edema with pitting, extending to the thighs, with tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with partial response to treatment; persistent sputum production raises concern for possible underlying infection or exacerbation. 2. Congestive heart failure with persistent fluid overload; current diuretic therapy remains insufficient. 3. Ongoing insomnia, pending sleep study; current pharmacological management requires reassessment.
PLAN
1. Review chest X-ray results; no evidence of pneumonia, but mild hyperinflation consistent with COPD exacerbation. 2. Continue oral prednisone 40 mg daily for an additional 5 days to manage airway inflammation. 3. Maintain furosemide at 320 mg daily, with close monitoring of renal function and electrolytes; consider adding spironolactone for persistent edema management. 4. Continue nebulized albuterol every 2 hours and nebulized budesonide every 6 hours; add ipratropium bromide for enhanced bronchodilation. 5. Expedite the sleep study referral and consider adjustment of insomnia management strategy, potentially introducing gabapentin for sleep disturbances if necessary. 6. Reinforce the importance of adherence to the treatment plan and monitoring for any acute changes in symptoms, including daily weight checks and reporting any significant fluid retention.
Mr. Fairfax acknowledged the treatment plan adjustments and expressed understanding of the need for continued monitoring and follow-up.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was stable for discharge, with a follow-up appointment scheduled for 08/28/29. He was advised to seek immediate medical attention for any acute exacerbations of respiratory distress, chest pain, or sudden weight gain.
